subject: EU→US Data Export: Operational checklist & evidence requested
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cambridgehealth.co.uk>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: julian.marks@cambridgehealth.co.uk
Date: 2026-10-29T08:14:00Z
Subject: Initial request: operational evidence for EU→US processing

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — Cambridge Health is moving quickly on the integration planning. As part of our internal DPO review we need a short operational checklist and supporting evidence for EU→US data exports tied to the Redwood-hosted inference flows (model logs, token traces, customer prompts). Our security team has flagged the following asks:

- Confirm whether Personal Data (as defined in our DPA) is ever stored outside EU regions and for how long (retention windows).
- Provide the Transfer Impact Assessment/high-level mitigations (SCCs mapping, pseudonymization details, encryption at rest/in transit).
- Provide an inventory of KMS integrations and whether keys are customer-managed (HSM/KMS).
- Evidence of SOC 2 controls mapping to CAIQ/SIG responses for cross-border controls.

We appreciate any attachments (checklist, logs extract, SCCs execution scan). Our timeline: internal DPO review by Nov 10 — can you confirm whether you can deliver before then?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Elena Rossi
DPO, Cambridge Health Solutions
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cambridgehealth.co.uk>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial request: operational evidence for EU→US processing

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal/contracting) and Karthik (security/infrastructure) to provide consolidated artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- Data residency & retention: Redwood’s hosted API stores prompt/response traces in EU by default for customers who choose EU regions; for customers using our US region there is a routed replica for serving only — we retain token traces for up to 30 days by default; retention is configurable per-account. (Will provide export of retention config and an anonymized sample.)
- SCCs & TIA: we maintain a Transfer Impact Assessment summary and SCCs mapping table. We will provide the TIA operational checklist and the SCCs execution log.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations on Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted customers keys are Redwood-managed by default. Karthik will confirm specifics and attach a KMS inventory.
- SOC2/CAIQ/SIG evidence: Marissa will attach the control mappings and the sections most relevant to cross-border processing.

We aim to deliver the checklist + supporting artifacts by EOD Nov 3 so you have time before Nov 10. If you need a signed exhibit (SCCs execution page) we can send a DocuSign link.

Action items (from our side):
- Karthik: produce KMS inventory + brief technical TIA summary (attachments).
- Marissa: extract SOC2/CAIQ cross-border control mappings and redact cert details as needed.
- Olga: produce operational checklist PDF and sample redacted logs.

Happy to schedule 30 min on Monday to walk the DPO team through the artifacts.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cambridgehealth.co.uk>, Julian Marks <julian.marks@cambridgehealth.co.uk>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial request: operational evidence for EU→US processing

Folks — attaching the technical pack. Summary pasted below; see attachments: redwood_tia_operational_checklist.pdf, scc_execution_log.csv, kms-inventory.xlsx.

Summary (technical):
- Export scope: For hosted EU-region customers, production inference traffic and short-term KV cache remain in EU; asynchronous analytics pipelines (metrics, aggregated usage) may traverse to US analytics clusters for processing. Token traces that are retained for debugging are pseudonymized (user identifiers replaced with internal IDs) unless the customer elects to persist raw prompts.
- Retention: Default traces retention = 30 days; retention TTL is configurable per-account (can be set to 0).
- Encryption: Data in transit TLS1.2+, at-rest encryption using AES-256 (Redwood-managed KMS by default). Dedicated/Private customers can use customer-managed KMS keys (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys on request. KMS inventory attached.
- SCCs mapping: we document where each SCC clause is addressed (technical, contractual, operational). The scc_execution_log.csv includes the last execution audit (2026-07-19) and controls owners.
- DPIA mitigations: pseudonymization, narrow retention windows, strict role-based access to token logs, automated deletion hooks when account termination occurs, and contractual commitments to refrain from model training on customer prompts.
- Logs sample: redacted sample included; all samples are sanitized and hashed.

If Cambridge needs a signed exhibit for SCCs we can route a DocuSign envelope with the SCP exhibit + appendix that lists operational controls. I’ve added a short checklist in the first attachment that maps items to evidence files.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs: redwood_tia_operational_checklist.pdf; scc_execution_log.csv; kms-inventory.xlsx)
From: Julian Marks <julian.marks@cambridgehealth.co.uk>

Cc: elena.rossi@cambridgehealth.co.uk, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Initial request: operational evidence for EU→US processing

Thanks — that package looks comprehensive and the timeline works. Two quick follow-ups before we close the ticket:

1) Can you send the DocuSign link for SCCs exhibit (we require an executed copy in our vendor file)?
2) For the KMS inventory: can you confirm whether Redwood-managed keys ever have access outside Redwood infrastructure teams (i.e., are they accessible to any cloud vendor staff)? A short statement is sufficient.

If you can get the DocuSign link and a brief KMS access statement by close of business Nov 6 we’ll be able to complete our DPO sign-off. Appreciated.

—Julian
Head of Vendor Risk, Cambridge Health Solutions
